title: Projection exchange and scalar trace determine the normalized exceptional mate
statement: For ordinary derived sheaves with arbitrary Grothendieck abelian symmetric monoidal coefficients, fix a Cartesian square, compact-support functors L and L prime, pullbacks H and J, and right adjoints R and R prime with adjunctions. Let P and P prime be natural projection transformations, with P invertible, and b:L;H isomorphic to J;L prime. Let W and W prime be coefficients with l:J W isomorphic to W prime and scalar traces t:L W to the unit and t prime:L prime W prime to the unit. Suppose gamma and gamma prime are invertible natural transformations from twisted pullback to R and R prime, normalized by P,t and P prime,t prime. Assume the scalar trace square for b,l,t,t prime and the raw projection exchange equation for b,P,P prime and the canonical pullback tensor and square comparisons. Then the mate of b inverse is invertible at every input K, and J gamma_K followed by that mate equals the canonical tensor-pullback comparison followed by l tensor the square comparison, followed by gamma prime at H K.

proof.text: Projection naturality in l extends the supplied raw projection-exchange square to the coefficient comparison. Tensor-pullback naturality and the left-unitor comparison tensor the scalar trace equation with any K.

Extract the two homogeneous counit equations from IntegrationGammaNormalized. Paste the preceding two squares. The projection P at W,K is invertible, as is its pullback; cancel it and b to obtain the counit square. Supply epimorphism instances directly from the known isomorphisms.

Apply the inverse adjunction Hom equivalence. The mate-counit identity and naturality of b identify the two transposes, proving the desired equality. The two gamma components and the source comparison are invertible, so the equality and cancellation imply invertibility of the mate.
